chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thal'abah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Aqra' (menses-free period) are the pure ones.
ai.seo_question: What does the term Al-Aqra' refer to in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the legal definition of 'Al-Aqra'' as the intervals of ritual purity between menstrual cycles, affirming their status as 'Al-Athkar' (the pure ones). This definition is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining when a woman is permitted to perform Salah and other acts of worship, distinguishing the state of purity from the state of major ritual impurity (Janabah or Hayd).

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hajjal, from sa’alba, from Zurara,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
A- Aqra’a, these are the pure ones’.
